messages:
talia: hey team, talia here  just started this morning. Running through k8s onboarding but `kubectl get pods -n model-training` returns `Forbidden`. I followed the kubeconfig steps in the doc but i'm seeing two redwood contexts (redwood-prod and redwood-dev) and i'm not sure which to use. who should I ping to get read access to the training namespace?

jamie (devex): welcome @talia! :wave: For training namespaces we usually give view access to the `modeling-team` group. Pinging @devops-ian to check the quickest path. Do you need to port-forward or exec today?

talia: just need to view logs and list pods today; may need port-forward later this week.

devops-ian: hi @talia, i'll help. first run `kubectl config get-contexts` and `kubectl config current-context` and paste results. If your current context is `redwood-prod` switch to `redwood-dev` first — training lives in dev for new hires. Also check `echo $KUBECONFIG` in case you have extra merged configs.

leah (eng): fwiw i had a similar issue day 2 — my kubeconfig had an old `kubeconfig.local` merged and it pointed to the wrong cluster. `grep -n "server:" ~/.kube/config` helped me spot it.

talia: current-context is `redwood-prod` (oops). `kubectl config get-contexts` shows `redwood-prod`, `redwood-dev`, and `minikube`. KUBECONFIG empty. Switched to `redwood-dev` and still Forbidden.

ops-bot: INFRA-1299 created by devops-ian: "Onboard talia: temp RoleBinding view for talia in model-training". ETA: 15m.

devops-ian: thanks. i'm going to apply a temporary RoleBinding in `model-training` for your SSO user `talia@redwood.ai`. that should let you list pods and read logs. If you need port-forward later we'll do a scoped permission. YAML i'm applying:

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: onboarding-view-talia
  namespace: model-training
subjects:
- kind: User
  name: "talia@redwood.ai"
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: view
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

apply should be immediate. After that run `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n model-training --as talia@redwood.ai` then `kubectl get pods -n model-training`.

talia: `can-i` -> yes, and `kubectl get pods -n model-training` lists pods now. thanks! :tada:

jamie (devex): great. i'll add a line in the onboarding checklist: "switch to redwood-dev for training namespaces" and a note to check merged kubeconfigs. linking doc: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/k8s-setup (added screenshot).

devops-ian: follow-up note: this binding is temporary (72 hours). we'll onboard you to the `modeling-team` SSO group so you get permanent access. if you need port-forward permission before the group is set up, reply here and i'll add a scoped role for port-forward.

leah (eng): if you want a quick map of common namespaces and which teams own them, ping me — happy to do a 10-min walkthrough.

talia: yes please, that would be awesome. thanks everyone for the quick help!"
